main_mystery: Who is conning whom, and who dies?
truth: The wife engineered the entire hire to frame the housekeeper for the husband's murder, choosing her precisely because her criminal past makes her disposable and believable as a killer. The husband is not the predator; he is the target. The housekeeper is also running a con (she came to rob or blackmail this family), but the wife's con is deeper and older. The deepest betrayal: the one ally the housekeeper (and the reader) trusted most is the trap.

red_herrings.description: The husband is the predator / murderer of the previous housekeeper
The husband's locked office contains evidence of his crimes
The previous housekeeper was murdered by the husband

major_reveals.name: Tier 1 False Answer Established
major_reveals.description: Reader fully believes the husband is the threat. The wife is a fragile prisoner. The housekeeper is an innocent victim.

major_reveals.name: Tier 2 False Answer: Husband Murdered Previous Housekeeper
major_reveals.description: Reader concludes the husband murdered Clara Higgins. Evidence points hard at him. Housekeeper commits to protecting the wife.

major_reveals.name: Tier 3 First Real Lift: Housekeeper Is Also a Con Artist
major_reveals.description: The housekeeper's hidden agenda is revealed to the reader. Her 'innocence' was a performance. The reader must re-read every earlier action as consistent with a con.

major_reveals.name: Tier 3 First Real Lift: Wife Is the Architect
major_reveals.description: The wife is revealed as the architect of everything. Her fragility was a performance. The reader must re-read every earlier kindness as manipulation.

major_reveals.name: Tier 4 True Reveal: The Frame Job
major_reveals.description: The wife engineered the entire hire to frame the housekeeper for the husband's murder. Physical evidence proves it. The husband is the target, not the predator.

clues.description: The husband speaks to the wife in a cold, condescending tone. He controls her medications and visitors.
clues.note: Re-read: This is the husband's genuine frustration with his wife's manipulation, not control.

clues.description: The wife has a bruise on her wrist that she claims is from the husband.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife inflicted this on herself to maintain the fragile victim facade.

clues.description: The wife knows too much about the housekeeper's past — mentions her hometown and a specific job she had five years ago.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife researched the housekeeper thoroughly before hiring her.

clues.description: The locked room at the end of the hall. The wife says it's the husband's office and he keeps it locked.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife controls access to this room. It contains her planning materials.

clues.description: A neighbor mentions the previous housekeeper, Clara Higgins, 'left suddenly' and 'was never the same after working there.'
clues.note: Re-read: Clara left because she discovered the wife's plan and fled.

clues.description: The housekeeper finds a photograph of Clara hidden in a drawer. Clara looks scared. The husband is in the background.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife planted this photo to implicate the husband.

clues.description: The husband has a violent temper — he throws a glass against the wall during a dinner party argument.
clues.note: Re-read: The husband's temper is real, but it's a reaction to his wife's long-term gaslighting.

clues.description: The housekeeper overhears the husband on the phone saying 'She's getting too close. We need to handle it.'
clues.note: Re-read: The husband is talking about his wife's manipulation, not the housekeeper.

clues.description: A police detective visits the house asking about Clara Higgins. The husband is evasive. The wife is visibly nervous.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife is nervous because she planted evidence against the husband that might be discovered.

clues.description: The housekeeper pockets a small silver spoon from the kitchen on her first day.
clues.note: Re-read: This is the first sign of her hidden agenda. She is a thief.

clues.description: The housekeeper lies about her criminal record on the job application. She claims she's never been arrested.
clues.note: Re-read: She has a history of fraud and theft. The wife knew this when she hired her.

clues.description: The housekeeper snoops through the husband's study when he's away, looking for financial documents or valuables.
clues.note: Re-read: She is there to rob or blackmail the family, not to save the wife.

clues.description: The wife asks the housekeeper very specific questions about her past, her skills, and her fears — framed as 'getting to know you.'
clues.note: Re-read: The wife is assessing the housekeeper's suitability as a patsy.

clues.description: The wife has a hidden drawer in her bedroom with a ledger of names, dates, and amounts of money.
clues.note: Re-read: The ledger contains the names of past targets and the housekeeper's name with a date.

clues.description: The wife's 'fragility' seems to fluctuate. She is weak when the husband is home, but strong and sharp when he is away.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife's fragility is a performance for the husband and the housekeeper.

clues.description: The wife tells the housekeeper a story about a woman she knew who was framed by her husband. The details are eerily specific.
clues.note: Re-read: The wife is describing her own plan to the housekeeper, testing her reaction.

clues.description: The housekeeper finds a copy of her own criminal record in the locked room, with notes in the wife's handwriting.
clues.note: This is the first piece of physical evidence that proves the wife's plan.

clues.description: A knife from the kitchen has the housekeeper's fingerprints on it. The housekeeper never used that knife.
clues.note: The wife planted the housekeeper's fingerprints on the murder weapon early in the story.

clues.description: The housekeeper finds a letter, apparently written by her, confessing to a plan to kill the husband. The handwriting is forged.
clues.note: The wife forged the letter. It is planted in the housekeeper's room.

clues.description: The wife's diary, hidden in the locked room, details her plan: 'Subject 7 is perfect. Disposable. Believable. The police will see her record and stop looking.'
clues.note: This is the definitive physical evidence. The wife's own words prove the con.

clues.description: A bank statement shows a large withdrawal from the wife's account on the day the housekeeper was hired — payment for the forged documents and the planted evidence.
clues.note: This confirms the wife's financial investment in the frame job.
